Score a completed Skat game

Source: R/score.R
sk_score_game.Rd

Determines whether the declarer won and by how much, given the declarer's card points, whether they took every trick, the complete scoring value, and the game type.

Usage

sk_score_game(
  declarer_points,
  game_type,
  game_value,
  declarer_won_all = FALSE,
  declarer_lost_all = FALSE,
  call = rlang::caller_env(),
  schneider_announced = FALSE,
  schwarz_announced = FALSE,
  ouvert = FALSE
)

Arguments

declarer_points

Card points (0-120) the declarer collected in tricks, including the skat, even in a hand game.

game_type

A single game-type string, one of sk_game_types().

game_value

The complete value including achieved/announced levels (see sk_game_value()). It is not a bid; overbidding is resolved externally.

declarer_won_all

Logical; TRUE if the declarer took every trick (relevant for schwarz). Defaults to FALSE.

declarer_lost_all

Logical; TRUE if the declarer took no trick at all. Defaults to FALSE. For null games this determines the outcome directly.

call

The calling environment, used for error reporting.

schneider_announced, schwarz_announced

Logical; contract requirements. Schwarz announced implies schneider announced. Defaults to FALSE.

ouvert

Logical; suit/grand ouvert requires every trick. Null ouvert retains the no-trick objective. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A list of class sk_result with elements:

  • won: logical, did the declarer win;

  • schneider: logical, was schneider reached (declarer to 90 or defence held to 30);

  • schwarz: logical, was schwarz reached (one side took every trick);

  • game_value: integer, the complete scoring value;

  • score: integer, points credited to the declarer – the game value if won, twice the negated game value if lost.

Details

The declarer needs 61 of the 120 card points to win a suit or grand game. Reaching 90 (or holding the defence to 30) is schneider; taking every trick is schwarz. Null games invert the goal: the declarer wins only by taking no trick at all, and neither schneider nor schwarz applies. A lost game costs twice the game value.

See also

sk_game_value() computes the scoring value; sk_play_game() calls this on a played-out deal.

Examples

sk_score_game(72, "hearts", game_value = 20)
#> <sk_result>: declarer won
#> • Game value: 20
#> • Score: 20
#> • Schneider: no
#> • Schwarz: no
sk_score_game(59, "hearts", game_value = 20)  # lost, did not reach 61
#> <sk_result>: declarer lost
#> • Game value: 20
#> • Score: -40
#> • Schneider: no
#> • Schwarz: no
sk_score_game(0, "null", game_value = 23, declarer_lost_all = TRUE)
#> <sk_result>: declarer won
#> • Game value: 23
#> • Score: 23
#> • Schneider: no
#> • Schwarz: no
